note: The authorities the rijal books cite by a one-word name («قال النجاشي», «ذكره الكشي», «قال الشيخ»), and the men they are. They stand in few chains or none, so how often the chains name a man cannot tell a reader who types «النجاشي» or «الكشي» that he means the author of the Rijal and not his ancestor or another man of the same nisba; how often the books cite him can. index_people.py counts the citations in the entries it serves (cited_count); the names are set by hand, checked 2026-11-10. «known_as» are the names a scholar knows the man by that the books do not head him with (al-ʿUrayḍī, al-Shaykh al-Ṣadūq, Thiqat al-Islām): added to his titles and English names. And an authority's cited name found among another man's titles — «الصدوق» on Ibn Qūlawayh, from «روى عنه الصدوق» — is taken off him. «only_his» (2026-11-11) are names that belong to that man alone: names_only_his() takes them off any other man's names and titles — the Tanqīḥ reading gave «الشيخ الصدوق» to Ibn Qūlawayh. The two envoys are al-ʿAmrī: the learned map reads «العمري» as al-ʿUmarī, which the ʿAlawī ʿUmarīs are, so their English names are added here rather than the word changed.
